name: Dandelion

facts.what: Leaves, flowers, roots: the whole plant
facts.how: Young leaves raw, older cooked; flowers for fritters; roots roasted for tea
facts.when: Cool months in Texas, November through April
facts.value: Vitamins A and K, minerals; classic bitter green

caution: The only real hazard is the lawn itself: harvest nowhere herbicides are sprayed. Texas false dandelions are look-alikes but harmless.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A basal rosette of backward-toothed leaves, one hollow milky stem per flower, never branched. Everything similar in a Texas lawn is at worst just less tasty.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Pick young leaves before flowering for salads; wilt older ones with bacon and vinegar the way generations of grandmothers settled the bitterness argument.
